What a high score means: Can plausibly achieve required flow, pressure and pulsatile behaviour.
Rationale: Both have a plausible displacement-based route to the target. 1A must complete two sequential duties per circuit period; 1B gives each chamber a full period and a dedicated load. Neither complete architecture has demonstrated the operating envelope.

What a high score means: Can reproduce desired flow and pressure-waveform features under operating conditions
Rationale: 1A has shorter duty windows, state carry-over between loads and no overlap of direct chamber ejections. 1B permits overlapping cycles and separate chamber states. Its advantage remains conditional on suitable actuation, valve timing and circuit loads; linked commands do not provide arbitrary independent control.

What a high score means: Stable, measurable and capable of repeatable profiles
Rationale: Both can be instrumented, but neither has repeated-run evidence or a verified complete model. Retained-gas state, reservoir inventory, seals and valve switching must be controlled. Separate chambers alone do not prove better repeatability.

1A saves one piston/chamber assembly but adds circuit selection hardware and its control. 1B duplicates chambers and seals but retains dedicated paths. No comparable BOM or quotations support a cost difference.

What a high score means: Achievable with university equipment, accessible parts and manageable development effort
Rationale: 1A concentrates development in routing and sealing. 1B requires two chamber assemblies and coordinated motion. Drawings, tolerances, candidate parts and workshop availability have not established either as easier.

What a high score means: Suitable with BMF and does not degrade and limits unwanted effects on fluid properties
Rationale: Architecture alone cannot establish compatibility. Both require checks of wetted materials, seals, temperature, gas retention and changes in fluid properties against the selected BMF.

What a high score means: Disassembly possible, draining, cleaning and replacement of worn parts
Rationale: 1A has fewer chambers but a selector manifold may create difficult-to-drain passages. 1B has more wetted parts but dedicated circuits. Access, dead spaces, drainage and seal replacement need a layout assessment.

What a high score means: Can accommodate both systemic and pulmonary circulation interfaces
Rationale: Both can connect the two circulations. 1B has dedicated right/left interfaces and chamber states, with no reassignment of a shared chamber. 1A requires coordinated selectors and pressure-state carry-over. Reservoir balance remains necessary in both.

What a high score means: Low expected wear and good prospect of maintaining performance over the required duty
Rationale: The shared piston performs twice as many fill-eject duties per unit time as each dedicated piston at the same outlet pulse rate. This is an exposure difference, not a lifetime prediction: 1B has more seals/components and no wear data exist for either.

What a high score means: Low vibration, noise and disturbance to sensors or future optical measurements
Rationale: 1A has faster shared-chamber duty scheduling; 1B has additional moving parts and possible coupled forces. Mounting, balance, transmission, valve actuation and sensor installation remain unspecified. No measured vibration or noise comparison exists.
Scores are provisional and are not PDS pass/fail results.
